transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I've been having this strange problem lately when I talk to people. I work with jewelry, mostly repairs and custom settings, and a customer will ask me a really simple question, like when a ring repair will be ready. And I try to tell them, but my answer just starts going from the shop invoices to... well, to the garden soil. I was working on my flower beds last weekend because the hydrangeas are just looking so sad this year, the soil is all wrong and we haven't had enough rain. 

But anyway, I'll go from the invoices to the garden soil, and then somehow I'm rambling to this poor customer about my mortgage papers. And I can just look at their faces and see them losing me completely. They just look so confused. So... yeah, I guess that's why I made the appointment.
Do you feel anxious or stressed when you start talking about unrelated topics to your customers?

Anxious? No, I don't really feel stressed when it's happening. I usually just feel like I'm having a normal conversation, you know? Like I'm just explaining things as they come to me. Like the other day, I was trying to explain to a woman how we size a platinum band. Platinum is so tricky, it requires a much higher melting point than gold. My uncle Arthur used to say gold was the only real money anyway. He kept all these heavy gold coins in a big floor safe in his basement. That basement always smelled like damp cedar and powdered laundry detergent. I actually tried to find that exact same detergent at the grocery store last week because the smell just reminded me of him, but all they have now are those little plastic pods. Do you use those pods? I always worry they're terrible for the local water supply, all that plastic just dissolving into the rivers...
Does this kind of conversation, where you jump from one topic to another, happen to you in other areas of your life, not just at work?

Well, yeah, it's not just at work. Like I was saying when I first got here, I came in because it's just... it's happening a lot. Someone will ask me a simple question, you know, like when a ring repair will be ready, and my answer just starts going from the shop invoices to the garden soil to the mortgage papers. And I can just see them losing me. It happens with my sister on the phone, too. She called to ask if I was coming to Sunday dinner, and the next thing I know, I'm talking about how the postal worker always leaves my mail on the porch step instead of in the box. Which is a real problem, actually, because if it rains, the envelopes get completely soaked, and then you can't even read the return address. I had a letter from the bank get ruined that way once. But anyway, yeah, I can just see people's faces, or hear it in their voice on the phone, that they have no idea how I got from point A to point B. It's just... frustrating, I guess.
Are you finding that this way of talking is causing problems in your relationships with family or friends?

Well, it's definitely causing problems at work, which affects everything else. I mean, my husband has had to start double-checking all my invoices, and I used to handle all of that myself for years. He’s an accountant, actually, so he’s good with numbers. He works for a firm downtown, near that really good Italian bakery. They make these cannolis with the little chocolate chips on the ends, the kind that are really crisp, not soggy. I hate a soggy pastry. It just ruins the whole experience with coffee. I usually take my coffee black, though sometimes a little cream if it's too bitter. 

But anyway, yeah, I've had to cut way back on my custom jewelry work because I keep losing track during the client consultations, and I've been missing deadlines for repairs. It's just hard to keep it all straight right now.
Are you having trouble completing tasks or chores at home because of this way of talking or thinking?

At home? Um... no, not really. I mean, the chores still get done. I usually just do the laundry and load the dishwasher, and that doesn't really take much focus. Though, our dishwasher has been making this awful grinding noise lately right in the middle of the wash cycle. I think one of the plastic lids from my food storage containers fell down and melted onto the heating element. You know how that smells, just awful, like burning chemicals. It reminds me of the time they were tarring the roof at the strip mall where my jewelry shop is. The smell was so strong we had to keep the front door propped open all day, which was a total nightmare for security. We have a chime on the door, but still, you never know who's going to walk in off the street when it's just wide open like that. There was this one guy who came in looking for a watch battery and he had this huge golden retriever with him... but anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, chores. No, I don't think I'm having trouble finishing them.
Do you find it hard to focus on what you're doing when you're not talking to someone?

When I'm not talking to someone? Um... it's not as noticeable, I guess. If I'm just sitting quietly at my workbench setting a stone, my hands kind of just know what to do. Like I told you a few minutes ago, the whole reason I even came in here is because of what happens when I actually have to answer somebody. Like I said before, they'll ask a simple thing about a ring repair, and I end up bouncing from the shop invoices to the garden soil to the mortgage papers. 

And speaking of the mortgage papers, we actually just refinanced last year, which was a huge headache because the appraiser the bank sent out tracked mud all over my good hallway runner. It's a woven wool Persian rug, so you can't just use regular carpet cleaner on it or it ruins the dyes. You have to let the mud dry completely and then brush it out with a special bristle brush. I actually found that rug at an estate sale a few years back. The woman running the sale was wearing this gorgeous vintage turquoise brooch, real Sleeping Beauty turquoise, you don't see that color much anymore... but, um, wait, what did you just ask me? Oh, focusing when I'm alone. Yeah, I think I'm mostly okay when I'm by myself, it's just when I have to talk to people that everything gets so scrambled.
Are your friends or family members commenting on or reacting to your way of talking?

Yeah, they definitely are. I mean, my husband has been looking at me like I have two heads lately. And my clients, too. Like I was saying, that's exactly why I came in here. When somebody asks me a simple question, like, "When will my ring repair be ready?" my answer just... it starts going from the shop invoices to the garden soil to the mortgage papers. And I can just see them losing me. Their eyes kind of glaze over. 

It reminds me of the look my sister gives me when I try to explain the different grades of silver. She only ever buys sterling, which is fine, but she doesn't understand that fine silver is softer and better for certain types of bezel settings. I made her this beautiful pendant for her birthday last year with a piece of sea glass she found on vacation in Maine. Maine is just gorgeous in the fall, isn't it? The leaves turning all those incredible colors. We drove up the coast a few years ago and stopped at this little roadside stand that sold wild blueberry jam. I bought three jars and we ate it on everything. Toast, pancakes, even stirred it into oatmeal. Oatmeal is so good for you, my doctor told me it helps lower cholesterol, which I guess I need to watch since I'm getting older... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right. People reacting to me. Yeah, I can see it on their faces. They just look confused.
Are you having any difficulty remembering things or learning new information outside of your conversations with others?

Remembering things? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, outside of talking to people, my memory seems fine. I haven't had any trouble learning new things, either. Like, I just learned this new technique for flush setting tiny diamonds. It's really tricky because if you push the metal too hard, you can chip the stone, and diamonds might be hard, but they can still cleave if you hit them at the wrong angle. 

Actually, I had a client bring in her grandmother's engagement ring last month, an old European cut diamond, and it had this tiny little chip right on the girdle. She wanted me to reset it into a bezel to hide the chip, which is smart, honestly. Bezels are so much more secure than prongs anyway. Prongs always catch on sweaters. I ruined my favorite cashmere cardigan last winter because my ring caught on the sleeve. It was this beautiful dusty rose color, too. I tried to pull the snag through to the inside, but you could still see where the knit was pulled tight. Cashmere is so delicate, you really have to hand wash it with baby shampoo. Regular detergent strips the natural oils out of the wool. My mom taught me that. She used to knit these incredible afghans... um, what was the question? Oh, memory. No, my memory is fine as long as I'm just working on my own.
Do you feel like your way of talking is causing you a lot of stress or emotional upset?

Stress? Yeah, it really is. It's... it's actually messing up my business. I've had to cut way back on custom work because I keep missing repair deadlines. And when I sit down for client consultations, I just lose track of everything we're discussing. It's gotten so bad I have to have my husband double-check all the shop invoices that I used to handle all by myself. 

He's been really good about it, though. He usually does the grocery shopping on Tuesdays while I'm at the shop, and he always remembers to get those little mandarin oranges I like. The ones in the netting? They're so sweet right now. Citrus is really best in the winter anyway, which seems backward, doesn't it? You'd think summer for fruit, but no, winter is citrus season. We had a lemon tree when I was growing up in California, right in the backyard. You could just walk out and pick a lemon for iced tea. My mother used to make sun tea in this huge glass jar on the patio. She'd put mint in it, too. Mint grows like a weed, though, you really have to plant it in a pot or it takes over the whole garden. I tried growing it here, but the soil... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, stress. Yeah, it's incredibly stressful having to rely on my husband for the invoices and messing up my custom work. It just feels like I'm losing my grip on the shop.
Are you finding it difficult to complete tasks or make decisions on your own because of the way your thoughts are organized?

Yeah, completing tasks is... it's getting really hard. Like I was saying before, I've had to cut way back on my custom work. I just keep missing the repair deadlines because I can't stay on track. And the client consultations are a mess, I completely lose the thread of what they want. It's so frustrating because I've always prided myself on my custom designs. I used to sketch everything out by hand on this beautiful vellum paper. 

Vellum is so nice to draw on, it has this smooth finish but it holds graphite perfectly. I buy my pencils from this little art supply store downtown. It's one of those great old shops with creaky wooden floors and it always smells like linseed oil and cedar. Cedar is such a comforting smell, isn't it? My grandfather had a cedar chest where he kept all his old wool blankets. He was in the Navy, so he had these heavy, scratchy surplus blankets. He was stationed in San Diego for a while, which is such a beautiful city. The weather is just perfect all year round. We went to the zoo there once when I was a kid, and I remember seeing the flamingos and thinking it was so strange that they turn pink from what they eat. Shrimp, I think it is? Or algae? It's funny how diet can change your color. Like if you eat too many carrots, you can turn orange. I read that somewhere... 

Wait, sorry, what were you asking about? Oh, right, making decisions and doing things on my own. Yeah, it's bad. I can't even trust myself with the shop invoices anymore. I used to do all the bookkeeping myself, but now my husband has to double-check every single one of them because my thoughts are just all over the place.
Are you feeling like your way of talking and thinking is straining your relationships with your family and friends?

Yeah, it definitely is putting a strain on things, especially with my husband. Like I said, I'm having to lean on him so much more now. I've had to cut way back on my custom work because I just keep missing repair deadlines, and I completely lose track of what's happening during client consultations. And then having to ask him to double-check all the shop invoices... I used to handle all of that myself, no problem. 

He's been patient, but I know it's a lot for him to take on. He already works full time at the hardware store. It's that local one on Main Street, not one of the big box places. I really prefer the smaller stores, you know? The people who work there actually know what they're talking about. Like last week, we needed a new washer for the kitchen faucet because it was dripping. Just drip, drip, drip all night. It was driving me crazy. Water torture is a real thing, you know. I read about it in this history book about medieval punishments. They used to do some horrible things back then. The iron maiden, the rack... history is just so full of violence. It makes you wonder how humanity survived at all. Sometimes I watch those historical documentaries on PBS, the ones with the slow panning across old photographs. Ken Burns, I think? His Civil War one was incredible. The letters they wrote back then were so poetic. People don't write letters anymore, it's all text messages and emails. There's no romance in an email... 

Um, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, my husband. Yeah, it's just hard on him having to pick up my slack with the invoices and everything because my brain just won't cooperate anymore.
Are you having trouble following instructions or recipes when you're alone?

Yeah, recipes are getting really tough. It's honestly just like what I keep telling you about the shop. I just can't follow the steps in order anymore. It's exactly why I've been cutting back on the custom jewelry pieces and why my husband is stuck double-checking all those invoices I used to do in my sleep. I try to read a recipe and I just lose my place, kind of like how I completely lose track of what's going on during my client consultations. 

I tried to make a pound cake on Sunday. It's supposed to be simple, right? But I couldn't remember if I'd already added the baking powder. My grandmother used to make the best pound cake in this incredibly heavy cast iron bundt pan. Cast iron is great, but you have to season it perfectly or everything just glues itself to the bottom. You have to rub it with oil and bake it upside down. I prefer olive oil for cooking most things, but it has a low smoke point, so it's not good for high heat. Avocado oil is much better for that. Avocados are so expensive lately, though. I saw them for three dollars each at the farmer's market last weekend. The market is really nice right now, they have all these heirloom pumpkins out. Some of them are covered in those weird bumps, they look almost like warts, but they're so decorative. People put them on their front porches with dried corn stalks and hay bales. I'm actually allergic to hay, it makes my eyes water so badly... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, following instructions alone. Yeah, I just can't keep the steps straight anymore. It's exactly why I keep missing my repair deadlines at work. I just get completely lost in the middle of doing things.
Are you finding it hard to enjoy your hobbies or leisure activities because of the way your mind is jumping from one thing to another?

Yeah, it's... it's just not the same anymore. I used to love hunting for old clasps, you know? Going to estate sales and antique shops just to find these unique, vintage pieces to incorporate into my work. And I used to plan these little jewelry classes for beginners, which was always so much fun. But lately, I mostly just stare at the trays of materials and feel like none of it is worth starting. It's just too much effort. 

Estate sales are really interesting, though. You get to walk through someone's entire life, basically. All their old furniture, their books, the china they probably only used on Thanksgiving. I always wonder what happens to the things that don't sell. Do they just throw them away? It seems like such a waste. We throw away so much in this country. Landfills are just overflowing. I saw a documentary about how much plastic is in the ocean, and it's terrifying. There's this massive patch of garbage just floating out there in the Pacific. It's hurting the sea turtles. Turtles are fascinating creatures, they live for such a long time. Some tortoises can live to be over a hundred years old. Imagine seeing a whole century pass by. The changes you'd witness... the invention of airplanes, the internet... 

I'm sorry, I'm drifting again. What did you ask me? Oh, right, my hobbies. Yeah, I just don't have the drive for it right now. I look at my tools and the stones, and I just feel empty about it all. It's like the spark is completely gone.
Do you find that your way of talking and thinking is consistently causing problems for you, regardless of whether you're at work, with family, or out in public?

Yeah, it really is causing problems everywhere. Like I keep saying, it's just... it's affecting everything. I’ve had to cut way back on my custom work because I just keep missing repair deadlines. And when I sit down for client consultations, I just completely lose track of the conversation. And then there's the shop invoices... I used to handle all of that myself, no problem at all, but now I have to have my husband double-check every single one. 

He's been so good about it, but he has his own work, you know? He works at that hardware store, and they sell these amazing little brass hinges. Brass is such a beautiful metal to work with. It tarnishes, though, if you don't polish it. I have this special polishing cloth I keep at my bench, it's impregnated with this rouge compound. The rouge gets all over your fingers, makes them look like you've been eating raspberries. I love fresh raspberries, especially with a little bit of cream. My grandmother used to grow them along the back fence of her yard. The birds would always try to get to them first, so she had to put up this shiny netting to scare them away. Crows are really smart, though, they figure out how to get past the netting. I read somewhere that crows can actually remember human faces and hold grudges. Imagine a bird holding a grudge against you! It's kind of funny, but also a little creepy. Like, what if they tell all their crow friends about you? They call a group of crows a murder, which is such a strange term...

Wait, I'm sorry, I completely lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, right, causing problems. Yeah, it's just really frustrating because I can't even get through a consultation or an invoice anymore without getting completely lost.
Do you feel like your way of talking and thinking is affecting your overall quality of life?

Yeah, it really is. It's just... it's pulling the rug out from under everything. Like I've been saying, I'm cutting way back on my custom jewelry pieces because I just can't trust myself to hit the repair deadlines anymore. And the client consultations are a mess, I just lose the thread of what they're asking for. And the shop invoices... I used to fly through those, and now my husband has to sit down and double-check every single one of them. 

He's so patient with me, but I know it's a burden. He has this old leather armchair he likes to sit in when he does the paperwork. It's so worn out, the leather is cracking on the armrests. We should probably get it reupholstered, but you know how hard it is to find a good upholsterer these days. There used to be this little shop down on Main Street, run by this older Italian gentleman. He did beautiful work, completely restored a velvet chaise lounge for my mother years ago. Velvet is so tricky to clean, though. You can't just use water, it ruins the pile. You have to use a dry solvent. Solvents always smell so harsh, like gasoline or something. I hate the smell of gasoline. It always reminds me of this time my car broke down on the side of the highway in the middle of summer. The heat radiating off the asphalt was just suffocating. You could see the heat waves shimmering in the air, making everything look like a mirage. Like you're in the desert...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my quality of life. Yeah, it's just really hard right now. I feel like I'm losing my grip on the business, needing help with the invoices and messing up the consultations. It's just not how I want to be living.
Do you feel like your way of talking and thinking is consistently interfering with your daily activities, no matter where you are or what you're doing?

I know I probably sound like a broken record today, but yes, it really doesn't matter where I am or what I'm doing. It's constantly getting in the way. Like I was saying before, my daily routine at the shop is just completely derailed. I've had to step way back from taking on new custom work because I just keep blowing right past my repair deadlines. And trying to sit with a client for a consultation is nearly impossible because my brain just checks out and I lose the thread of what they want. And having my husband double-check every single invoice I write... it's just my everyday reality now. 

He uses this specific red pen when he checks them. It’s one of those fine-tip felt pens. I love the way those write, they just glide over the paper. Paper manufacturing is actually a really fascinating process, if you think about it. They have to pulp the wood and press it out into these massive, continuous sheets. I visited a paper mill once on a school field trip when I was a kid. The smell was absolutely awful, kind of like sulfur or rotten eggs. I can't stand the smell of sulfur. It reminds me of those hot springs out west. My parents took me to Yellowstone when I was ten, and we saw Old Faithful erupt. It's amazing how the earth just builds up all that pressure and has to release it like that. Geothermal energy could probably power so much more of the grid than we use it for. We rely way too much on fossil fuels, and the gas prices are just ridiculous lately. I went to fill up my tank on Tuesday and I couldn't believe how much it cost to just get a half tank...

Oh, gosh, I'm sorry. I'm completely off track again, aren't I? What did you ask me? Right, my daily activities. Yes, it's just a constant struggle, whether I'm trying to talk to a client or just finish a simple jewelry repair on time. It's exhausting not being able to just do my normal routine.
Have you noticed that this way of talking and thinking has been consistent over the past few months, or are there times when it seems to get better or worse?

Honestly, it's been pretty constant. There aren't really good or bad days with it anymore, just this steady fog. This whole change has been going on since not long after we took on the business mortgage, so almost two years now. 

Getting that mortgage was such a nightmare, the paperwork was just endless. We had to go into the bank branch over and over to sign things, and they always had those little glass bowls of lollipops on the teller counters. I always took the butterscotch ones. Butterscotch is such an underrated flavor, don't you think? I used to make butterscotch pudding from scratch when my kids were little. You have to temper the egg yolks just right, though, or it turns into sweet scrambled eggs, which is just a complete disaster. My youngest hated eggs anyway, wouldn't touch them unless they were completely hidden in a cake. Baking a cake from scratch takes so much time, and you have to make sure the butter is perfectly room temperature. If it's too cold, it just clumps up in the sugar and ruins the whole texture of the crumb. It makes the cake so dense, almost like a pound cake, which is fine if you're making a pound cake, but... 

Oh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm sorry, my brain just drifts off. You were asking if it gets better or worse? Yeah, no, it's just been consistently like this for about two years now, ever since that mortgage.
Are you in danger of losing your job at the jewelry shop because of these difficulties with conversation and focus?

Well, I mean, it's my own shop, so I can't exactly fire myself, but... the business is definitely suffering. Like I've been saying, I've had to really cut back on taking new custom pieces because I just keep blowing past the repair deadlines. And sitting down for client consultations is just a disaster, I completely lose track of what they're asking for. Plus needing my husband to double-check every single invoice that I used to just breeze through... it's bad. 

He's been working so much extra to help me out. He usually wears these blue flannel shirts when he comes into the shop on weekends. Flannel is so cozy, especially when the weather starts to turn. We get such beautiful autumns here, the leaves turn those gorgeous shades of red and gold. I love driving up through the mountains when the leaves are changing. The roads get so winding up there, though. You really have to be careful, especially if it's rained and the wet leaves are stuck to the pavement. It can be just as slippery as ice. I slid on some ice once when I was first learning to drive. My dad was in the passenger seat and he yelled so loud I almost jumped out of my skin. He always had a really booming voice, he used to sing in a barbershop quartet... 

I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, losing my job. Right. Well, since it's my business, I won't get fired, but I feel like I'm losing the shop anyway because I just can't do the work I used to do. I can't meet the deadlines or handle the consultations or the invoices anymore.
Do you feel like your difficulties with conversation and focus are affecting your relationships with your loved ones?

Well, yes, I think it is. My husband... he's just so frustrated with me. I mean, he's trying to be patient, helping with the invoices and everything, but I can see the toll it's taking on him. He looks so tired lately. He’s been drinking so much coffee to keep up. We have this old French press at home that we use every morning. It makes such a strong cup, way better than those drip machines. The glass beaker on it cracked once, though, and it was surprisingly hard to find a replacement part that fit just right. We had to go to three different specialty kitchen stores. I always end up buying more than I need when I go into those places. They have all those shiny copper pots hanging from the ceiling. Copper is so beautiful, but it tarnishes so quickly if you don't keep it polished. I work with copper sometimes at the shop, mostly for practice pieces or wire wrapping. Wire wrapping is actually really therapeutic, it's just repeating the same motions over and over. It's kind of like knitting, I guess. My grandmother used to knit these incredible afghans... 

Wait, what was the question? Relationships? Oh, right. Yes, it's definitely putting a strain on things with my husband, and my kids too, honestly. I just can't seem to stay present when they're talking to me.
Do you feel like your difficulties with conversation and focus are making it hard for you to maintain your relationships with friends and family outside of work?

Well, I guess... I mean, I don't really know. I don't see my friends as much as I used to, but everybody gets busy, right? My friend Sarah, she just had her first grandbaby, a little girl. They named her Lily. Lily is such a sweet name for a baby. We have daylilies growing along the fence in our backyard, the bright orange ones. They spread like crazy, though, you really have to stay on top of dividing them every few years or they just take over the whole garden bed. I used to love gardening, getting my hands dirty in the soil. There's this one type of potting soil that smells so earthy and rich, almost like a forest after it rains. The smell of rain on dry pavement is actually called petrichor, did you know that? I read that in a magazine at the dentist's office once. The dentist always plays that soft rock station, it's so soothing...

I'm sorry, did you ask about my friends? I just... I haven't really noticed if it's the talking thing that's keeping them away, or if we're just all getting older and busier. I just don't know.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the impact of the symptoms on social relationships with friends and family outside of work. While this relates to functional impairment, the patient's specific manifestation for functional impairment focuses on occupational difficulties and has already been discussed. There are no other matching symptom items for this specific question.

patient.answer:
Well, I guess... I mean, I don't really know. I don't see my friends as much as I used to, but everybody gets busy, right? My friend Sarah, she just had her first grandbaby, a little girl. They named her Lily. Lily is such a sweet name for a baby. We have daylilies growing along the fence in our backyard, the bright orange ones. They spread like crazy, though, you really have to stay on top of dividing them every few years or they just take over the whole garden bed. I used to love gardening, getting my hands dirty in the soil. There's this one type of potting soil that smells so earthy and rich, almost like a forest after it rains. The smell of rain on dry pavement is actually called petrichor, did you know that? I read that in a magazine at the dentist's office once. The dentist always plays that soft rock station, it's so soothing...

I'm sorry, did you ask about my friends? I just... I haven't really noticed if it's the talking thing that's keeping them away, or if we're just all getting older and busier. I just don't know.

inference.note: R47.0 was ruled out as the patient's symptoms are more consistent with difficulties in sustaining attention and following through on instructions, rather than a specific speech or language disorder.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of consistently jumping from one topic to another, difficulty staying on track in conversations, and trouble following instructions or recipes, along with the significant impairment in social and occupational functioning, are most consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), predominantly inattentive type.
